statusDetail: Coverage-complete audit across homepage, section, article, and invalid-route recovery. Noticias subdomain returned Access Denied, so equivalent www.uol.com.br sports templates were used. Search, authenticated account, subscription checkout/cancellation, and payment were not covered because they require broader cross-property or credentialed flows.

page.notes: Large Brazilian news portal. Core content is server-rendered. Distinct legacy homepage and responsive article/section templates show inconsistent behavior.

paths.description: Homepage and primary news-discovery surface; desktop, narrow viewport, preference emulation, keyboard focus, performance, security, network, accessibility and memory.
Sports section listing, representing section/index templates and the consent-entry experience.
Current sports article, representing article/detail templates and the core reading journey.
Invalid URL used to inspect HTTP/not-found recovery behavior.

findings.summary: System dark mode is ignored
findings.evidence: The dark-condition screenshot is visually the same white interface as the default and the feature probe found zero prefers-color-scheme rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven light/dark surface and text tokens.

findings.summary: Motion continues under reduced-motion preference
findings.evidence: With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce active, 13 animations remained running with durations of 1 to 3 seconds.
findings.suggestedFix: Use prefers-reduced-motion to remove non-essential animation and auto-advance while preserving state feedback.

findings.summary: No explicit high-contrast adaptation
findings.evidence: The CSS feature probe found no prefers-contrast or forced-colors rules; the high-contrast screenshot retained the same low-emphasis chrome.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors and prefers-contrast adaptations for essential text, focus, controls, and scroll affordances.

findings.summary: Route changes do not use View Transitions
findings.evidence: Rendered HTML and accessible CSS contained no view-transition or startViewTransition usage across the homepage navigation surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance eligible same-origin navigation with cross-document View Transitions and reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Long news feed has no scroll-state guidance
findings.evidence: The homepage is 17,705 CSS pixels tall, while the feature probe found no scroll-state queries or scroll-timeline indicator.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight reading/scroll position affordance or responsive sticky chrome that reacts declaratively to scroll state.

findings.summary: Consent modal blocks the section before content can be used
findings.evidence: Fresh sports loads are covered by a modal on desktop and mobile; body scrolling is locked and the dialog describes sharing with 211 partners.
findings.suggestedFix: Make the consent surface compact and content-first, with equivalent accept/reject controls and access to content without unnecessary interruption.

findings.summary: Consent overlay is a custom div rather than a modal primitive
findings.evidence: The consent probe found role=dialog on a DIV without aria-modal; no dialog or popover primitive exists on the homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a native dialog where modality is required, with correct focus containment, Escape/cancel handling, and an explicit close/reject path.

findings.summary: Advertising and service chrome crowds the primary news content
findings.evidence: The desktop first viewport gives roughly 300px to a blank advertising slot plus multiple header rows before the lead headline, and the mobile page remains dense.
findings.suggestedFix: Collapse empty ad inventory, reduce stacked navigation chrome, and move the lead content higher.

findings.summary: Mobile layouts are broken or scaled down
findings.evidence: The homepage forces a 1210px layout viewport at 360px, while the article reports 85px horizontal overflow and visibly overlaps the title, navigation, currency, and subscription controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Use width=device-width, fluid intrinsic layouts, and responsive header composition; eliminate the article overflow at 320 to 400px.

findings.summary: Shared components do not adapt to their available space
findings.evidence: The feature probe found no container queries, and the article header components overlap at 360px instead of re-composing.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable header/article components containment and size-aware styles, with viewport fallbacks where needed.

findings.summary: Several controls are too small or lose visible focus
findings.evidence: Homepage focus sampling found top navigation links only about 14px high and multiple links/inputs with outline none; some controls are 24x24.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide at least 24x24 CSS-pixel targets (prefer 44x44), preserve visible :focus-visible styling, and avoid hover-only affordances.

findings.summary: The mobile article reading journey is obstructed
findings.evidence: At 360px the article headline and header controls overlap, the page is wider than the viewport, and the cookie banner obscures the opening paragraphs.
findings.suggestedFix: Repair the responsive article header and use a non-obscuring consent surface so reading can proceed immediately.

findings.summary: Invalid URLs silently become the homepage
findings.evidence: A deliberately invalid path redirected to https://www.uol.com.br/#404 but displayed normal homepage content, with no not-found heading, explanation, search, or recovery state.
findings.suggestedFix: Return a real 404 status and a clear not-found page with search, relevant links, and a route back to the homepage.

findings.summary: Homepage load performance misses the user-centric bar
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 6.7s, Speed Index 10.1s, TTI 17.2s, and performance score 0.56.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP content, defer ads and non-critical third parties, and break up interaction-blocking work.

findings.summary: Main-thread work causes blocking tasks
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 280ms TBT; the trace found four long tasks, up to 113ms, and 99.89ms trace TBT.
findings.suggestedFix: Split long tasks and defer low-priority ad, analytics, and player initialization until needed.

findings.summary: Resource delivery is dominated by scripts and third parties
findings.evidence: The HAR captured 192 requests and 2.61MB transferred, including 56 scripts/1.90MB; fonts took about 2.1s. Parser-discovered candidates were confirmed async where sampled, but the network dependency volume remains high.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a route-level resource budget, delay non-critical advertising/analytics, optimise font delivery, and cache the uncached player script.

findings.summary: Nearly 900KiB of JavaScript is unused on load
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 897KiB unused JavaScript, led by player, advertising, analytics, consent, and bidding bundles.
findings.suggestedFix: Conditionally import the player and advertising stacks only when their surfaces become eligible or visible.

findings.summary: Accessible names and roles are incomplete
findings.evidence: axe found critical missing image alt, two unnamed links, 24 prohibited ARIA uses, and focusable controls inside aria-hidden carousels; the DOM probe found unlabeled email/password inputs.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix names and labels, remove prohibited ARIA, and make hidden carousel slides inert.

findings.summary: Many text elements fail WCAG contrast
findings.evidence: axe reported 54 color-contrast failures, including weather text and promoted headline text.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust foreground/background design tokens to meet WCAG AA in every state.

findings.summary: Document structure and focus semantics are unreliable
findings.evidence: axe found no main landmark, incorrect heading order, empty headings, non-unique/nested landmarks, and aria-hidden focusable carousel content.
findings.suggestedFix: Add one main landmark, repair heading hierarchy/landmarks, and remove hidden slides from sequential focus.

findings.summary: Article text is not legible at a common mobile width
findings.evidence: At 360px the article title is covered by header/navigation controls and body content is clipped/obscured.
findings.suggestedFix: Recompose the mobile header and article grid so headings and body copy have an unobstructed single-column reading measure.

findings.summary: Reflow and target sizing fail on mobile
findings.evidence: The article overflows by 85px at 360px and homepage target sampling found links around 14px high and 24x24 controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Support 320px reflow without two-dimensional scrolling and enlarge interactive targets.

findings.summary: Third-party integrations log runtime failures
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured CORS errors and failed Adnxs network requests in the console.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove or correct failing bidder requests and handle optional third-party failures without console errors.

findings.summary: Asset markup creates avoidable risk
findings.evidence: The images audit found 90 of 100 images missing dimensions, 21 below-fold images not lazy-loaded, and two missing alts; axe also flagged a delayed meta refresh.
findings.suggestedFix: Add intrinsic image dimensions, lazy-load non-critical images, repair alt text, and remove the delayed meta refresh.

findings.summary: The page blocks BFCache and has source-map defects
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found an unload handler that blocks BFCache and missing/broken maps for large first-party/player JavaScript.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace unload with pagehide/visibility lifecycle handling and publish valid production source maps.

findings.summary: A login action is not crawlable and homepage mobile metadata is non-responsive
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found an anchor without href, and the homepage viewport is hard-coded to width=1210 rather than device width.
findings.suggestedFix: Use real href destinations for navigation and a device-width viewport with responsive CSS.

findings.summary: Cookie and response protections are incomplete
findings.evidence: Although HTTPS, HSTS, and frame-ancestors are present, X-Content-Type-Options is missing and all 19 observed cookies were flagged insecure by the primitive; several analytics/consent cookies lack Secure.
findings.suggestedFix: Set Secure and appropriate SameSite on every cookie and add nosniff; expand CSP beyond frame-ancestors to meaningful script/object/base controls.

findings.summary: The page activates an exceptionally broad tracking surface
findings.evidence: The tracker probe saw 62 third-party origins and 12 known trackers; the HAR attributed 185/192 requests and 2.44MB to non-main origins, while consent copy names 211 partners.
findings.suggestedFix: Block non-essential vendors before affirmative choice, reduce partners drastically, and batch/minimise measurement events.

findings.summary: The exposed sign-in form lacks modern input/auth affordances
findings.evidence: The homepage sign-in markup exposes email/password fields with no autocomplete tokens and no WebAuthn/passkey signal was observed.
findings.suggestedFix: Add correct username/current-password autocomplete and offer passkey sign-in/upgrade where account infrastructure permits.

findings.summary: Defensive browser policies are only partial
findings.evidence: Headers lack Permissions-Policy and nosniff; Referrer-Policy remains no-referrer-when-downgrade, and CSP only specifies frame-ancestors.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt a restrictive CSP, Permissions-Policy, nosniff, and strict-origin-when-cross-origin or stricter referrer policy.

findings.summary: HTTP failure recovery is misleading
findings.evidence: An invalid URL is rewritten to #404 and then renders ordinary homepage content rather than a clear error and recovery state.
findings.suggestedFix: Preserve the 404 status and provide an explicit error state with recovery actions.

findings.summary: Consent choice is asymmetric and tracking begins before a clear rejection
findings.evidence: The first consent layer offers Consent and Manage options, but no equally prominent Reject choice; it describes 211 partners. The homepage fallback says continued browsing is agreement and offers only OK.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide Reject all alongside Accept all with equal prominence, default non-essential purposes off, and do not infer consent from browsing.

findings.summary: Sign-in fields omit autocomplete assistance
findings.evidence: The DOM probe found email and password inputs with empty autocomplete values and no programmatic labels.
findings.suggestedFix: Use labelled fields with username and current-password autocomplete tokens; support password managers and passkeys.

findings.summary: Image delivery misses responsive efficiency basics
findings.evidence: Of 100 images, 90 lacked dimensions, 40 lacked srcset, 21 below-fold images were not lazy, and four were oversized.
findings.suggestedFix: Add dimensions, responsive srcset/sizes, lazy loading for below-fold media, and modern formats where seven legacy assets remain.

findings.summary: The page performs substantial work unrelated to immediate content
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 897KiB unused JS and the HAR recorded 64 fetch/XHR requests on initial load.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate background analytics, bidding, consent, and media work on visibility, consent, and user intent.

findings.summary: Third-party code dominates the page budget
findings.evidence: Third parties accounted for 185 requests and 2.44MB of 2.61MB transferred; 62 third-party origins were observed.
findings.suggestedFix: Set and enforce a third-party budget, remove low-value vendors, and lazy-load media/advertising integrations.

findings.summary: Public article content is deliberately unavailable to most AI agents
findings.evidence: Content is server-rendered (89 to 97 percent crawler coverage), but robots.txt explicitly disallows major agent/search user agents and no structured WebMCP capability is exposed.
findings.suggestedFix: If agent access is an intended channel, define an explicit agent policy and expose safe, read-only structured capabilities or feeds rather than blanket scraping.

findings.summary: Homepage memory footprint is disproportionate for a news index
findings.evidence: The baseline heap contained 1,318,836 nodes and 61.1MB self size before user interaction, with 236,636 closures.
findings.suggestedFix: Lazy-initialize non-visible modules and third parties, release unneeded closures, and set a memory budget for the homepage.
